job.title: 1st Shift - QC Operator
job.description: 2nd Shift - Quality Control (QC) Operator Location: Bristol, IN Â Shift: 2nd Shift â€“ 2:00pm-10:30pmÂ Training on 1st: 5:45am-2:15pm Â Pay: $20.00â€“$21.00 per hour, depending on experience Job Summary Are you detail-oriented, quality-driven, and someone who takes pride in making sure things are done right? We're seeking a dependable Quality Control (QC) Operator to join our team in Bristol, IN! In this role, you'll serve as one of the final checkpoints in the production process, inspecting finished cabinet components made from particle board before they are packaged and shipped to customers. This position requires the ability to evaluate products from both a technical and visual standpoint. You'll compare completed parts against their corresponding work orders to verify that specifications are correct, while also inspecting the overall appearance and finish of each piece to ensure it meets customer expectations. Because this position is located near the end of the production line, your attention to detail is critical. You'll help prevent incorrect, damaged, or visually unacceptable products from reaching the customer. Previous quality control or inspection experience is a huge plus, especially in a manufacturing or woodworking environment! What Youâ€™ll Be Doing As a Quality Control Operator, your core responsibilities will include: -Technical Inspection: Verify that completed parts match the specifications listed on their corresponding work orders. Ensure the correct components, dimensions, and details are present before the product moves forward.-Work Order Verification: Compare finished products against production documentation to confirm that each part is technically correct and meets the required specifications.-Visual Quality Inspection: Inspect cabinet components for scratches, dents, chips, damage, imperfections, and other visible issues that could affect the finished product.-Final Quality Checkpoint: Serve as one of the last quality control stops before products are shipped, helping ensure only acceptable products reach the customer.-Defect Identification: Recognize parts that do not meet technical or aesthetic standards and identify issues that need to be addressed.-Production Communication: Communicate quality concerns and discrepancies to the appropriate production personnel so issues can be corrected before shipment.-Attention to Detail: Carefully examine each piece to ensure it meets both the company's quality expectations and the customer's requirements. In addition, you will also be expected to maintain an organized inspection area, follow established quality procedures, and help support a consistent production workflow. What Weâ€™re Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications:Previous quality control, quality inspection, or manufacturing experience strongly preferredAbility to train on 1st Shift Schedule for 1-2 weeks as needed.Ability to read and interpret work orders and compare them against finished productsStrong attention to detail and excellent visual inspection skillsAbility to identify technical discrepancies and visible product imperfectionsComfortable working in a fast-paced production environmentAbility to communicate quality concerns clearly and professionallyAbility to follow inspection procedures and established quality standardsReliable attendance and punctualitySkills:-Technical Accuracy: Able to compare finished parts against work orders and verify that products meet the required specifications.-Visual Inspection: Has a keen eye for scratches, dents, chips, surface imperfections, and other cosmetic defects.-Attention to Detail: Thoroughly inspects each component rather than relying on a quick visual glance.-Quality Awareness: Understands the importance of catching errors before products reach the customer.-Documentation & Interpretation: Comfortable reading production paperwork and using it to verify that the correct product has been manufactured.-Communication: Able to clearly identify and report discrepancies so production issues can be addressed promptly. What Weâ€™re Looking For in a Candidate The ideal candidate is extremely detail-oriented, observant, dependable, and quality-focused. We're looking for someone who understands that quality control involves more than simply checking whether a product looks acceptable. They must be able to verify that the part is technically correct according to its work order while also ensuring it meets visual quality expectations. Previous QC experience is a huge advantage! Candidates who have worked in manufacturing inspection, cabinet production, woodworking, furniture manufacturing, or other quality-focused production environments are strongly encouraged to apply. This position requires someone who takes ownership of their inspections, stays focused throughout the shift, and understands that their work directly impacts the quality of the products customers receive. Work EnvironmentThis position is located within a manufacturing facility producing cabinet components made from particle board. The QC Operator will work near the end of the production line, inspecting completed parts before they move on to packaging and shipment. The work involves frequent visual inspections, reviewing work orders, comparing product specifications, and identifying both technical and cosmetic defects. Candidates should be comfortable working in an active production environment while maintaining consistent attention to detail and inspection accuracy. job.description: Job Title: Customer Service Representative Reports to: Customer Service Manager Department: Customer Service Direct reports: None FLSA Status: Full time, Exempt Position Summary: The Customer Service Representative is the customer's main point of contact, from first inquiry through delivery. The role answers customer questions, enters and manages orders, coordinates quoting activity, keeps customers informed and resolves issues so each customer gets the right product, on time, with a great experience. Key responsibilities Customer inquiries and quoting Serve as the primary contact for customers and dealers by phone, email and in person, responding to inquiries promptly. Provide quotes, pricing, lead times and product information, working with sales and engineering on non-standard requests. Answer questions on order status, delivery dates and product use. Order management Enter, verify and confirm orders in the ERP system, checking specifications, pricing and ship dates for accuracy. Process order changes and confirm price and schedule impact with sales, manufacturing and the customer before work proceeds. Coordinate with purchasing, manufacturing and shipping to keep orders on schedule and give customers early notice of any delays. Coordinate delivery schedules with shipping, carriers and dealers. Issue resolution Manage customer expectations and resolve issues as they arise. Handle returns, warranty claims and freight damage claims through resolution. Work with finance on invoicing, credits and customer account questions. Improvement Keep customer records, order files and customer service procedures accurate and up to date. Capture customer feedback and share it with sales and operations to improve the overall customer experience. Qualifications High school diploma required; associate's or bachelor's degree in business or a related field preferred. 2+ years of customer service or order entry experience, preferably in a manufacturing environment. Proven ability to manage many orders and requests at once, accurately and on time. Experience working directly with customers to manage expectations, schedules and changes. Proficient with Excel, Word and Outlook. Excellent communicator via email, on the phone or Teams. Experience with ERP systems preferred. Ability to read basic drawings and product specifications preferred. Core competencies Customer focus: builds trust with customers, keeps them informed and handles problems calmly and promptly. Problem solving: gets to the root of customer issues and finds practical fixes quickly. Teamwork: works well with sales, manufacturing and shipping to get answers and keep orders moving. Attention to detail: catches errors in orders, specifications and drawings before they reach the plant floor. Organization: juggles many orders and requests at once without letting anything slip. Attitude: Be positive and collaborative. Clear communication: writes concise status updates and handles difficult conversations professionally. Follow-through: owns commitments and closes loops without being chased. Physical Demands & Work Environment: The characteristics described below are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Physical Demands: While performing duties of this job, would occasionally be required to stand, walk, sit, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, stoop or kneel, talk and hear, and use fingers and hands to feel objects, tools or controls. Work might entail significant time spent standing, exposure to extreme temperatures, enduring distracting/uncomfortable sounds and noise levels, as well as exposure to potentially hazardous conditions and equipment. Must occasionally lift and/or move up to 40 pounds. Employee may be required to climb stairs as needed to access various areas of the building. Specific vision abilities required include close vision, distance vision, depth perceptions, and the ability to adjust focus. Overtime may be necessary as work load’s dictate. This may include weekdays, weekends and/or holidays. Work Environments: Job requires dealing calmly and effectively with high stress situations. Employees may be subject to random drug and alcohol testing, pre-employment physical and background checks.

job.description:
Your employer’s ‘year’ for the purposes of the Earned Sick Time Act is:
Number of Employees Earned Sick Time Accrual Employer May Limit Use To: 10 or fewer employees Minimum Accrual Rate 40 hours in a year 11 or more employees 1 hour for every 30 hours 72 hours in a year 1 hour for every 30 hours
• Determined by Employer written policy earned sick time may be carried over from year to year or paid out. A business with 10 or fewer employees is not required to permit an employee to use more than 40 hours of paid earned sick time in a single year, employers with 11 or more employees are not required to permit an employee to use more than 72 hours of paid earned sick time in a single year.
• Earned sick time shall begin to accrue on the effective date of this law, or upon commencement of the employee’s employment, whichever is later.
• An employee may use accrued earned sick time as it is accrued. Newly hired employees may be subject to a 120 day wait period for use.
• An employer is in compliance with the act if it provides any paid leave in at least the same amounts as that provided under this act that may be used for the same purposes and under the same conditions provided in this act and that is accrued at a rate equal to or greater than the rate described in subsections (1) and (2) of Section 3 of the act. Paid leave includes, but is not limited to, paid vacation days, personal days, and paid time off.
Earned Sick Time Uses An employer shall permit an employee to use the earned sick time accrued for any of the following: • The employee’s or the employee’s family member’s mental or physical illness, injury, or health condition; medical diagnosis, care, or treatment of the employee’s mental or physical illness, injury, or health condition; or preventative medical care for the employee.
• If the employee or the employee’s family member is a victim of domestic violence or sexual assault, for medical care or psychological or other counseling for physical or psychological injury or disability; to obtain services from a victim services organization; to relocate due to domestic violence or sexual assault; to obtain legal services; or to participate in any civil or criminal proceedings related to or resulting from the domestic violence or sexual assault.
• For meetings at a child’s school or place of care related to the child’s health or disability, or the effects of domestic violence or sexual assault on the child; or
• For closure of the employee’s place of business by order of a public official due to a public health emergency; for an employee’s need to care for a child whose school or place of care has been closed by order of a public official due to a public health emergency; or when it has been determined by the health authorities having jurisdiction or by a health care provider that the employee’s or employee’s family member’s presence in the community would jeopardize the health of others because of the employee’s or family member’s exposure to a communicable disease.
• An employer shall not require an employee to search for or secure a replacement worker as a condition for using earned sick time.
Exercise of Rights • An employer or any other person shall not interfere with, restrain, or deny the exercise of, or the attempt to exercise, any right
protected under this act. • An employer shall not take retaliatory personnel action or discriminate against an employee because the employee has exercised a right
protected under this act. “Retaliatory personnel action” means any of the following: ? Denial of any right guaranteed under this act. ? A threat, discharge, suspension, demotion, reduction of hours, or other adverse action against an employee or former employee for
exercise of a right guaranteed under this act. ? Sanctions against an employee who is a recipient of public benefits for exercise of a right guaranteed under this act. ? Interference with, or punishment for, an individual’s participation in any manner in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under this
act. • An employer’s absence control policy must not treat earned sick time taken under this act as an absence that may lead to or result in
retaliatory personnel action.
Complaint Filing An employee affected by an alleged violation, at any time within 3 years after the alleged violation or the date when the employee knew of the alleged violation may file a complaint with the Wage & Hour Division.
*For precise language of the statute, see Public Act 338 of 2018, as amended Auxiliary aids, services and other reasonable accommodations are available, upon request, to individuals with disabilities.

job.title: Accounting Specialist
job.description:  PAGE \* MERGEFORMAT 2 AGS COMPANY AUTOMOTIVE SOLUTIONS, LLC Job Title:Material MoverReport To:Carlena GarciaDepartment/Group:Ops/DC/S&RPosition Type:Full-TimeLocation:MuskegonSchedule:Mon – Fri, 7am – 330pmSalary:$18.50 - $20/hrBonus Potential:4 - 10% of base annual salaryRemote:NABenefits:YesThe Material Mover is a key contributor in the AGS Distribution Center, responsible for the safe, accurate, and efficient movement of product through our DC operations. This includes receiving inbound freight, picking and preparing outbound orders, staging product for shipment, and maintaining an organized and compliant warehouse environment. This is a physical, fast-paced role that requires attention to detail, reliability, and a commitment to doing the job right the first time. The Material Mover works as part of a team to fulfill customer orders accurately and on schedule, supporting AGS’s reputation for quality and reliability that has been built over nearly a century.AGS Company Automotive Solutions is a trusted leader in the automotive aftermarket, proudly serving customers for 95 years. With a reputation for quality, reliability, and innovation, AGS provides a wide range of products including brake, fuel, transmission, and specialty lines that keep vehicles on the road and performing at their best. Headquartered in Muskegon, Michigan, AGS is committed to operational excellence and continuous improvement across manufacturing, distribution, and customer service. Our people are the foundation of our success, and we foster a culture guided by our core values: Give, Respect, Act, Innovate, and Lead. These values shape how we work together, support one another, and deliver excellence to our customers every day. By combining strong Midwestern roots with forward-thinking innovation, AGS continues to expand its reach across global markets, driving progress and delivering solutions that customers can trust. Give: "We commit to generosity in every action, sharing our time, knowledge, and resources to foster a collaborative and supportive environment." Respect: "We uphold a culture of respect, where every voice is valued, and diversity is celebrated, ensuring a welcoming and inclusive workplace." Act: "We take decisive action, guided by integrity and responsibility, to address challenges proactively and achieve our goals effectively." Innovate: "We embrace creativity and innovation, constantly seeking novel solutions and approaches to drive progress and stay ahead of the curve." Lead: "We lead by example, inspiring others through our dedication and passion, and strive to empower each team member to reach their full potential.” Key Responsibilities Receiving & Inbound Unload inbound shipments from trucks and trailers using manual and powered equipment. Verify incoming product against purchase orders, bills of lading, and packing lists; report discrepancies immediately. Inspect inbound freight for damage or shortage; document and escalate as required. Label, sort, and put away received product into designated storage locations accurately and promptly. Maintain receiving documentation in accordance with company procedures. Packing & Shipping Pack outbound orders in accordance with product specifications, customer requirements, and carrier guidelines. Apply appropriate labels, documentation, and packaging materials to outbound shipments. Assist in loading outbound trailers and vehicles safely and efficiently. Verify outbound shipments against manifests or shipping documents before release. Support on-time shipment of all daily outbound orders. Product Movement & Equipment Operation Move product safely throughout the DC using pallet jacks, hand trucks, and other material handling equipment. Operate forklifts or reach trucks as certified and assigned. Ensure all equipment is operated in compliance with safety standards and company procedures. Perform pre-shift equipment inspections and report any mechanical concerns to a supervisor. Handle all product with care to prevent damage during movement and storage. Inventory & Organization Maintain accurate and organized product storage in all assigned areas of the DC. Assist with cycle counts, physical inventories, and location audits as directed. Replenish forward pick locations as needed to maintain operational efficiency. Report inventory discrepancies, damaged stock, or location errors to the supervisor or inventory team. Keep all work areas, aisles, and staging zones clean, clear, and clearly labeled. Safety & Compliance Follow all safety procedures and wear required PPE at all times. Operate all material handling equipment in compliance with OSHA standards and company safety policies. Immediately report unsafe conditions, near-misses, or accidents to a supervisor. Participate in safety training, inspections, and continuous improvement activities. Maintain a clean, organized, and hazard-free work environment. Team Collaboration & Communication Work cooperatively with reviving, shipping, inventory, and transportation team members to meet daily goals Communicate proactively about delays, shortages, or issues that may impact outbound orders. Support new team members during onboarding and share knowledge willingly. Culture & Collaboration Share knowledge generously and support development of others Promote a culture of open communication, continuous learning, and shared responsibility for quality Participate in team building, training, and company-wide initiatives to strengthen engagement and performance Model AGS values in day-to-day interactions and decision-making Contribute to a workplace where people feel valued, supported, and empowered to succeed. What Success Looks Like A successful Material Mover ensures that product moves through the distribution center accurately, safely, and on time, every shift. Inbound freight is received, verified, and put away accurately and promptly. Orders are picked and packed with a high degree of accuracy, meeting established rate standards. Outbound shipments leave on time and complete, every day. The DC is organized, clean, and safe at the start and end of every shift. Equipment is operated safely with zero preventable incidents. Inventory counts are accurate and discrepancies are reported quickly. Your supervisor and teammates can count on you to show up and deliver, no follow-up required. Qualifications and Education Requirements Requirements High school diploma or GED required. Prior experience in a distribution center, warehouse, or fulfillment environment preferred. Ability to operate manual pallet jacks and hand trucks; powered equipment experience preferred. Ability to read and follow pick lists, shipping documents, work instructions, and labels accurately. Basic math skills for order verification and inventory counting. Strong attention to detail, accuracy in picking and documentation is essential in this role. Reliable attendance and consistent punctuality; the DC depends on every team member being present and ready. Ability to work at a sustained pace in a physical, fast-moving environment. Preferred Forklift or reach truck certification (AGS will provide training for the right candidate). Experience with RF scanning, voice-pick systems, or warehouse management systems (WMS). Familiarity with 5S, lean warehouse principles, or DC productivity metrics. Prior experience in automotive parts, aftermarket distribution, or industrial product fulfillment. Physical Requirements Ability to stand, walk, and remain on your feet for the duration of an 8–10 hour shift. Frequent lifting, carrying, pushing, and pulling of product up to 50 lbs; occasional team lifts above 50 lbs. Frequent bending, twisting, reaching, and stooping throughout the shift. Ability to operate powered industrial equipment including forklifts and reach trucks. Ability to work in a warehouse environment with variable temperatures, noise levels, and seasonal conditions. Good hand-eye coordination, manual dexterity, and spatial awareness in a busy DC environment. Perks & Benefits At AGS Company Automotive Solutions, we believe great work starts with taking care of our people professionally, personally, and physically. Our benefits are designed to support your health, growth, and overall well-being while fostering a culture where people genuinely enjoy coming to work. Health & Wellness Medical, dental, and vision insurance Short-Term Disability (STD) and Long-Term Disability (LTD) coverage Life insurance AFLAC supplemental insurance options Fitness membership benefit to support an active, healthy lifestyle Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential support and resources Growth & Development Ongoing educational and professional development opportunities Proud partner of Cornerstone University’s Soar Program, providing access to learning, leadership development, and career growth pathways Culture First A people-centered, values-driven culture rooted in respect, collaboration, and trust Supportive leadership that believes in growth, feedback, and doing the right thing A workplace where your voice matters and your contributions are recognized Salary & Bonus Base Salary Range: $18.50– $20/hr (Range is based on experience, skills, and role alignment within the organization.) Bonus Eligibility: Eligible for a performance-based bonus of up to 4 -10% of base annual salary, based on individual, team, and company performance. Why AGS? At AGS Company Automotive Solutions, you’re not just taking on a job, you’re joining a team that values people, teamwork, and doing things the right way. With more than 95 years in the automotive industry, AGS offers the stability of a well-established company while continuing to invest in innovation, operational excellence, and continuous improvement. Culture matters here. We lead with respect, communicate openly, and support one another across teams. On the production floor, that means working alongside people who are willing to share knowledge, help solve problems, and step in when something needs to get done. Whether you’re troubleshooting equipment, supporting operators, or improving how machines run, you’ll be part of a team focused on keeping operations safe, efficient, and reliable. This role plays an important part in keeping production running smoothly. Your ability to diagnose issues, make adjustments, and support the team directly impacts productivity, quality, and the success of our operations. If you enjoy hands-on work, solving mechanical challenges, and helping equipment perform at its best, this role provides the opportunity to make a real impact every day. We also believe growth should be supported, not left to chance. Through training, skill development, and partnerships with programs like Cornerstone University’s Soar Program, we encourage employees to expand their knowledge and continue developing throughout their careers. At AGS, we live our values - Give, Respect, Act, Innovate, and Lead - every day. If you’re looking for a place where teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement come together, AGS is a great place to grow your career. Salary progression is guided by demonstrated capability, impact, and readiness for expanded responsibility. This approach supports fairness, internal equity, transparency, and sustainable growth for both our people and the business.By signing below, I acknowledge that I have received, read, and understand the job description for the Production Supervisor position at AGS Company Automotive Solutions. I understand my responsibilities as outlined in this document and agree to perform the duties described to the best of my ability in alignment with the company's values and expectations.Agreed By:Date:Reporting Manager:Date: This document is confidential and intended for internal use only. v 1.0 – April 2026

job.title: Programmable Operator 2nd shift (TubeMatic)
job.description: Programmable Operator Location: Clare, MI Pay: $18.50 per hour Shift: 2nd shift Job Summary Are you a motivated and detail-oriented individual looking for a new opportunity? We're seeking a Programmable Operator to join our team in Clare, MI. In this role, you'll be a vital part of our operations, helping us to ensure quality production through robotic welding and CNC machine operation. What You'll Be Doing As a Programmable Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Inspecting Incoming Material: Ensuring quality specifications and quantities are met. Operating an Overhead Crane: Receiving and issuing raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas. Robotic Welding and CNC Machine Operation: Programming, setting up, operating, and adjusting process variables to meet quality demands. In addition, you will also be expected to maintain inventory control, complete entry of work orders and packing slips, and perform daily shift maintenance inspections. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent desired. Two years of experience and/or educational related courses on related machinery. Experience/knowledge of blueprint reading, AutoCAD, CNC programming, thermal cutting machinery, and welding knowledge preferred. Ability to obtain a Crane License and fork truck license. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret the English language. Satisfactory math skills including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and basic geometry. Excellent problem-solving abilities. Ability to multi-task. Ability to operate machinery on a three-dimensional basis. Agility of the upper and lower body extremities, and capable of lifting 50 pounds regularly. Skills: Quality Inspection: To ensure incoming material meets specifications. Inventory Management: To maintain inventory control by identifying and labeling raw material. Computer System Entry: To complete entry of work orders, packing slips, etc. into the main computer system. Welding Knowledge: To perform tasks related to robotic welding and fabrication. Blueprint Interpretation: To select appropriate programs and verify part specifications. Precision Measurement: Utilizing calipers, micrometers, and other measuring devices to verify accuracy. Problem Solving: To address any problems regarding safety, quality, production, or inventory issues. Collaboration: To confer with Team Leaders, Crew Leaders, and Engineering Programmers. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth. We're seeking a Material Handler to join our team in Clare, MI. In this role, you'll be a vital part of our operations, helping us to provide support to production associates by receiving, dispensing, and accurately maintaining inventory in a safe, clean, and organized work area. Capable of lifting 50 pounds regularly and up to 75 pounds on occasion. Skills: Work Area Organization: Maintaining a safe, clean, and organized work area. ERP System Proficiency: Utilizing the ERP system for all transactions. Inventory Management: Assisting with maintaining inventory levels for vertical storage units (VSU) and assuring accurate inventory levels by correctly backflushing work orders. Issue Reporting: Reporting any unplanned issues to the Team Leader. Component Preparation: Pulling together all non-floor stock components that are in the VSU for work orders, including printing any labels that are needed. Hardware Receiving and Placement: Receiving hardware into the VSU unit placement in proper storeroom location and sequence. Collaboration: Conferring with the Team Leader or Crew Leader on work orders and job orders for the delivery of hardware. Material Transport: Utilizing a fork truck, carts, and other approved methods to transport materials between departments. Cycle Counting: Performing cycle counts on products and materials. job.title: Press Operator
job.description: Press OperatorLocation: Grand Ledge, MI Shift: 5:00 am – 3:30 PM Mon -Thu any OT will be on Friday.Pay: $17.27 Job SummaryWe’re looking for a reliable and detail-oriented Press Operator to join a busy molding and production team. In this role, you will operate presses, mix resin, prepare molds, inspect finished parts, and complete required documentation. The ideal candidate is safety-focused, mechanically inclined, and able to follow detailed production specifications. What You’ll Be DoingPour resin onto fiberglass sheets according to production specification sheets. Track production counts using counters and complete required paperwork. Clean molds using air hoses, apply mold wax, and prepare materials for production. Measure and mix resin and catalyst using dipsticks and air mixers. Operate presses safely and efficiently. Place fiberglass sheets into molds and verify part accuracy using fixtures and measurement tools. Work with robotics to verify water jet accuracy during first-part runs. Inspect parts for defects, perform minor repairs, and complete rework as needed. Adjust mold compression timing and temperature as instructed. Replace empty resin barrels and maintain clean buckets and molds. Conduct first-part runs, complete SPC charts, and obtain supervisor approval. Stamp parts with date and lot numbers. Clean resin run-out, gel coat, and machine beds. Record measurements on ratio logs and calculate mix ratios three times per shift. Report production numbers to supervisors. Troubleshoot production issues as part of a team. Review production boards to determine job numbers, lot numbers, and resin requirements. Spray adhesive and place tags as required. Complete Mix Ratio Logs and perform testing as needed per lab instructions. What We’re Looking ForQualifications:High school diploma or GED required. Ability to follow detailed work instructions and production specifications. Strong attention to detail and mechanical aptitude. Safety-focused and able to work in a fast-paced environment. Prior molding or finishing experience preferred but not required. Skills:Ability to operate presses and related molding equipment. Basic math and measurement skills. Ability to perform minor part repairs and quality checks. Strong teamwork and communication skills. Why Join Us?This is a great opportunity to grow your skills in a hands-on manufacturing environment while working with a team committed to quality, safety, and continuous improvement. job.title: 1st Shift - Manual Lathe Machinist (Eastern)
job.description: Manual Lathe Machinist, Up to $45/hr - Detroit, MI (1st Shift) Job Overview: We are seeking a skilled and experienced Manual Lathe Machinist to join our manufacturing team. The successful candidate will be responsible for setting up, operating, and maintaining manual lathe machines to produce high-precision metal components and parts. This position requires a strong attention to detail, the ability to read blueprints and technical drawings, and a solid understanding of machining processes. Key Responsibilities: Set up and operate manual lathe machines to machine parts and components as per specifications. Read and interpret blueprints, drawings, and technical documents to determine machining processes and specifications. Select and install appropriate cutting tools, fixtures, and attachments for the job. Monitor machine operations to ensure proper functionality and adherence to tolerances. Perform routine maintenance on equipment and troubleshoot mechanical issues. Inspect finished parts using various measuring tools such as micrometers, calipers, and gauges to ensure precision and quality standards are met. Maintain a clean and organized work area in accordance with safety guidelines. Collaborate with engineers and other team members to improve processes and product quality. Ensure that all work is completed within required timelines and meets production goals. Qualifications: Proven experience as a Manual Lathe Machinist or similar role in a manufacturing environment. Strong knowledge of machining techniques, materials, and tooling. Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, and schematics. Proficient in using measuring instruments (micrometers, calipers, etc.) to ensure quality control. Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills. Excellent attention to detail and ability to work with high precision. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Strong safety awareness and adherence to workplace safety procedures. High school diploma or equivalent; relevant technical certifications or vocational training a plus. Physical Requirements: Ability to stand for extended periods. Manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination required for machine operation. Preferred Skills: Experience with CNC lathes or other automated machinery. Knowledge of tool selection and programming. Familiarity with ISO and/or AS9100 quality standards. Let’s go to work! Apply online today or call our office at 734-284-2121. job.title: Grinder/General Labor
job.description: Essential Responsibilities Load and unload raw materials, castings, and finished products. Perform grinding, deburring, and finishing operations on brass and aluminum castings using hand grinders and other power tools. Remove excess material and inspect parts to ensure they meet quality standards. Assist machine operators with production tasks. Perform basic assembly, sorting, packaging, and labeling of products. Safely lift, carry, and move heavy materials and castings weighing up to 75 pounds, either independently or with assistance when required. Move materials throughout the facility using carts, pallet jacks, forklifts (if certified), or other material-handling equipment. Inspect parts for quality and report defects or concerns to supervisors. Maintain a clean and organized work area while following all company safety procedures. Follow work instructions, production schedules, and quality standards. Perform other general labor and manufacturing duties as assigned. Qualifications Previous manufacturing, foundry, or warehouse experience is preferred but not required. Experience using hand grinders or other power tools is a plus. Ability to work in a fast-paced manufacturing environment. Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality. Reliable attendance and punctuality. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Willingness to learn and follow all company safety procedures. Physical Requirements Frequently lift, carry, push, and pull up to 75 pounds. Stand, walk, bend, stoop, kneel, and twist throughout a 10-hour shift. Safely operate hand grinders and other power tools. Perform repetitive hand and arm movements while grinding and finishing castings. Must be able to wear a respirator and any other required personal protective equipment (PPE) for extended periods while performing assigned duties. Work in a manufacturing environment with heat, dust, moderate to high noise levels, and varying temperatures. Wear required PPE, including safety glasses, hearing protection, gloves, steel-toe boots, and other protective equipment as required.

In this role, you'll be responsible for operating industrial furnaces used in the heat treatment of steel and aluminum components. You'll play a critical role in ensuring products meet quality standards while maintaining safe and efficient production processes. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and stand for extended periods. Forklift experience or certification is a plus. Quality Focus: Ability to inspect parts and identify potential quality concerns. Safety Awareness: Commitment to following all safety procedures and PPE requirements. job.title: Production Opportunities (Marketing)
job.description: Production Opportunities Location: Clare, MI Pay: $18.50/hr Shift: All Shifts Job Summary Are you a motivated and detail-oriented individual looking for a new opportunity? We're seeking a Production Operator to join our team in Clare, MI. In this role, you'll be a vital part of our operations, helping us to ensure quality production through robotic welding and CNC machine operation. What You'll Be Doing As a Production Operator, your core responsibilities will include: Inspecting Incoming Material: Ensuring quality specifications and quantities are met. Operating an Overhead Crane: Receiving and issuing raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas. Robotic Welding and CNC Machine Operation: Programming, setting up, operating, and adjusting process variables to meet quality demands. In addition, you will also be expected to maintain inventory control, complete entry of work orders and packing slips, and perform daily shift maintenance inspections. Not only will you be responsible for inspecting and managing raw materials and operating an overhead crane, but you’ll also be primarily focused on robotic welding and operating other CNC machines, including programming, setup, and adjustment to ensure quality products. What We're Looking For To be successful in this role, you should have the following: Qualifications: High school diploma or equivalent desired. Two years of experience and/or educational related courses on related machinery desired. Experience/knowledge of blueprint reading, AutoCAD, CNC programming, thermal cutting machinery, and welding knowledge preferred. Ability to obtain a Crane License and fork truck license. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret the English language. Satisfactory math skills including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and basic geometry. Excellent problem-solving abilities. Ability to multi-task. Ability to operate machinery on a three-dimensional basis. Agility of the upper and lower body extremities, and capable of lifting 50 pounds regularly. Skills: Quality Inspection: To inspect incoming material for quality specification and quantities. Material Handling: To receive and issue raw material to and from saws, trucks, and storage areas by operation of an overhead crane. Robotic Welding and CNC Operation: Primary focus would be working on the robotic welder and fabrication of products utilizing other CNC machines, including programming, machine setup, operation, and adjustment of process variables to meet quality demands. Inventory Control: To maintain inventory control by identifying and labeling raw material with proper identification. Computer System Entry: To complete entry of work orders, packing slips, etc., into the main computer system. Welding Knowledge: Must be knowledgeable in welding. Work Order Processing: To receive and issue raw material according to the work order, prints, routings, and bill of lading. Program Selection: To select appropriate programs utilizing the operating software, based upon the work order and print. Verification: Cross-checking that revision, part number, and description are correct. Before loading material into the machine, verify correct amount, size, gauge, and length of material has been loaded into the machine and issued to the work order. Measurement: Utilizing calipers, micrometers, and other measuring devices to verify accuracy. Quality Assurance: To check the quality of the first part for appearance and that the part meets print specifications. Assures that the fit, function, and appearance of products are at, or exceed quality standards. Production Fulfillment: Fulfills production requirements. Part Placement: To place finished parts in proper container/rack and designated location. Record Keeping: To record on work order all labor and downtime, documenting all information pertaining to each work order and routing. Maintenance: Performs daily shift maintenance inspection per the preventative maintenance (PM) checklist. Collaboration: Confers with the Team Leader or Crew Leader on any problems regarding safety, quality, production, inventory issues, etc. Confers with Engineering Programmer to maximize potential efficiency and quality gains in the manufacturing process. Work Area Maintenance: Maintain high quality standards as regards to machine and work area. Removal of all metal scrap, debris, and residue from machine as needed. Why Join Us? This is an excellent opportunity for both short-term and long-term employment. We are committed to providing a supportive work environment and opportunities for growth.
